stem: A frequency distribution has class intervals 0-10, 10-20, 20-30, and 30-40, with frequencies 6, f, 10, and 4 respectively. The total frequency is 20+f and the arithmetic mean is 18. What is the value of f?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student divides the sum of (f x midpoint) products by the sum of the midpoints (80) instead of the total frequency, using the wrong denominator: (420+15f)/80 = 18 gives f = 68.
Student reads the stated mean as 19 instead of 18, solving (420+15f)/(20+f)=19 which gives 4f=40 and f=10.
Student correctly reaches 3f = 60 but divides by 4 instead of 3, computing 60/4 = 15 through an arithmetic slip.

explanation: Use midpoints: 5, 15, 25, 35. The weighted sum is 5x6 + 15xf + 25x10 + 35x4 = 420+15f. Set mean = weighted sum / total frequency: (420+15f)/(20+f)=18. Cross-multiplying gives 420+15f = 360+18f, so 3f=60 and f=20.

explanation_sections.punchline: f = 20. Setting up mean = Sum(f x midpoint)/Sum(f) and solving the resulting linear equation in f is the only correct method.
explanation_sections.approach: Assign midpoints to each class, form the equation mean = Sum(f_i x x_i)/N where N includes f, then cross-multiply and isolate f. Always use total frequency N as the denominator, never the sum of midpoints.
explanation_sections.lesson: The denominator in the mean formula is total frequency, not the number of classes or the sum of midpoints. Any denominator error changes the equation completely. Verify by substituting f back to confirm the mean.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds. Computing the known part of the weighted sum (30+250+140=420) takes about 20 seconds. Setting up and cross-multiplying the equation takes 30 seconds. Solving 3f=60 takes under 10 seconds. Use remaining time to substitute f=20 back and confirm mean=18.
